title: Passive Voice
summary: Use ser + participle and se-passives to focus on actions and results rather than agents.

sections.heading: Ser + past participle
sections.body: The analytical passive uses **ser + past participle**. The participle agrees with the subject in gender and number. This structure is common in news, formal reports, and written language.

examples.en: The decision will be announced tomorrow.

sections.heading: Agent with por
sections.body: When you mention the agent, use **por** or a contraction such as **pelo/pela**. Often the agent is omitted because it is unknown or unimportant.

examples.pt: O livro foi escrito por uma autora brasileira.
examples.en: The book was written by a Brazilian author.

examples.pt: A proposta foi aprovada pelo diretor.
examples.en: The proposal was approved by the director.

examples.pt: A janela foi quebrada durante a festa.
examples.en: The window was broken during the party.

sections.heading: Passive with se
sections.body: The **se** passive is common for general statements, signs, and announcements. The verb agrees with the thing being sold, done, or requested in standard usage.

examples.note: precisar de is impersonal and stays singular

examples.en: A commercial room is for rent.

keyPoints: Ser + participle focuses on the subject receiving the action.
Se-passives are common in signs and formal notices.

commonMistakes.wrong: O livro foi escrito pelo Machado de Assis.
commonMistakes.right: O livro foi escrito por Machado de Assis.
commonMistakes.note: Use por without article for many personal names.
In standard se-passive, verb agrees with plural subject.
